statement: A bag holds 3 kg of rice. How many portions of 250 g can be filled from it?

choices.misconception: I worked out how many 250 g portions fit in 1 kg, not in 3 kg.
I thought 250 g was half a kilogram.
I wrote 3 kg as 30,000 g, with one zero too many.
I multiplied 3 by 250 instead of dividing.

hints: How many grams are in a kilogram?
Put both amounts in the same unit before you divide. Then ask how many portions fit into the whole bag.
1 kg is 1,000 g, so the bag holds 3,000 g. Four portions of 250 g make 1,000 g.

solutions.reliable: 3 kg is 3 x 1,000 = 3,000 g. Each portion is 250 g, and 4 portions make 1,000 g, so 3,000 g fills 3 x 4 = 12 portions. The transferable idea: change to one unit first, then divide.
solutions.elegant: 250 g is a quarter of a kilogram, so each kilogram gives 4 portions and 3 kg give 12. The transferable idea: spot a friendly fraction of the bigger unit.

whyOnTest: Unit conversion between kilograms and grams, with the multiply-instead-of-divide and dropped-step slips offered.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
